claim: Actin dynamics generate forces to deform the membrane and overcome the cell's high turgor pressure during clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) in yeast.
source: Actin dynamics generate forces to deform the membrane and overcome the cell's high turgor pressure during clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) in yeast, but precise molecular details are still unresolved.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific understanding in the field, supported by the context of the manuscript.

claim: Previous models predicted that actin filaments of the endocytic meshwork continually polymerize and disassemble, turning over multiple times during an endocytic event.
source: Our previous models predicted that actin filaments of the endocytic meshwork continually polymerize and disassemble, turning over multiple times during an endocytic event, similar to other actin systems.
evidence: The authors reference their own prior modeling work.

claim: The overall lifetime of actin and actin-associated proteins in endocytic patches is approximately 20 seconds.
source: In contrast with the overall ~20 s lifetimes of actin and actin-associated proteins in endocytic patches, we detected single-molecule residence times around 1 to 2 s, and similarly high turnover rates of membrane-associated proteins in CME.
evidence: This is stated as a contrast to the new findings, representing prior knowledge.

claim: Single-molecule residence times of endocytic proteins are around 1 to 2 seconds.
source: In contrast with the overall ~20 s lifetimes of actin and actin-associated proteins in endocytic patches, we detected single-molecule residence times around 1 to 2 s, and similarly high turnover rates of membrane-associated proteins in CME.
evidence: This is a primary finding directly measured in the study.

claim: Membrane-associated proteins in CME show similarly high turnover rates as actin-associated proteins.
source: In contrast with the overall ~20 s lifetimes of actin and actin-associated proteins in endocytic patches, we detected single-molecule residence times around 1 to 2 s, and similarly high turnover rates of membrane-associated proteins in CME.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule tracking experiments.

claim: Many proteins in CME exhibit heterogeneous behaviors in their motions.
source: Furthermore, we find heterogeneous behaviors in many proteins' motions.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of single-molecule tracking data.

claim: Endocytic proteins turn over up to five times during the formation of an endocytic vesicle.
source: These results indicate that endocytic proteins turn over up to five times during the formation of an endocytic vesicle, and suggest revising quantitative models of force production.
evidence: This is calculated from the ratio of overall patch lifetime (~20s) to single-molecule residence time (~1-2s).

claim: The findings suggest that quantitative models of force production in CME should be revised.
source: These results indicate that endocytic proteins turn over up to five times during the formation of an endocytic vesicle, and suggest revising quantitative models of force production.
evidence: This is an interpretation and implication of the experimental findings.

claim: Clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) is the major pathway for eukaryotic cells to internalize plasma membrane and extracellular molecules.
source: Clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) is the major pathway for eukaryotic cells to internalize plasma membrane and extracellular molecules.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: In yeast, the invagination of a clathrin-coated pit (CCP) and formation of the ~50 nm vesicle relies on a dense meshwork of cytoskeletal actin filaments and associated proteins.
source: In yeast, the invagination of a clathrin-coated pit (CCP) and formation of the ~50 nm vesicle relies on a dense meshwork of cytoskeletal actin filaments and associated proteins (Goode et al., 2015; Kaksonen et al., 2003; Kaksonen et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The localized, rapidly-assembled actin meshwork is necessary to generate the force to bend the plasma membrane inward and overcome the cell's high turgor pressure.
source: This localized, rapidly-assembled actin meshwork is necessary to generate the force to bend the plasma membrane inward and overcome the cell's high turgor pressure (Aghamohammadzadeh and Ayscough, 2009; Boulant et al., 2011; Collins et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The understanding of the molecular machinery of CME is incomplete, especially in quantitative terms of how the endocytic assembly generates sufficient forces.
source: Although many endocytic proteins and their biochemical mechanisms have been characterized, our understanding of the molecular machinery is incomplete, especially in quantitative terms of how the endocytic assembly generates sufficient forces (Lacy et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The entire CME assembly is smaller than the optical diffraction limit (~250 nm).
source: CME is a challenging target for study because the entire assembly is smaller than the optical diffraction limit (~250 nm), the numbers of molecules at the site rapidly change, and most of the dynamics occur within ~20 s.
evidence: This is a statement about the physical characteristics of CME structures.

claim: The numbers of molecules at the CME site rapidly change.
source: CME is a challenging target for study because the entire assembly is smaller than the optical diffraction limit (~250 nm), the numbers of molecules at the site rapidly change, and most of the dynamics occur within ~20 s.
evidence: This is a statement about the dynamic nature of CME.

claim: Most of the dynamics in CME occur within approximately 20 seconds.
source: CME is a challenging target for study because the entire assembly is smaller than the optical diffraction limit (~250 nm), the numbers of molecules at the site rapidly change, and most of the dynamics occur within ~20 s.
evidence: This is a statement about the timescale of CME events.

claim: Theoretical modeling and novel imaging techniques have been necessary for detailed study of CME.
source: These unique challenges have made theoretical modeling and novel imaging techniques necessary for detailed study of CME (Berro and Lacy, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Quantitative microscopy studies have revealed a robust timeline of self-assembly in CME, as actin and associated proteins polymerize into a meshwork during invagination of the CCP and then gradually disassemble after the vesicle is pinched off.
source: Quantitative microscopy studies of the assembly and disassembly of endocytic proteins have revealed a robust timeline of self-assembly, as actin and associated proteins polymerize into a meshwork during invagination of the CCP and then gradually disassemble after the vesicle is pinched off (Berro and Pollard, 2014a; Kaksonen et al., 2003; Picco et al., 2015; Sirotkin et al., 2010; Taylor et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Recent super-resolution imaging and electron microscopy of CME sites have revealed increasingly detailed structural organization.
source: And while recent super-resolution imaging and electron microscopy of CME sites have revealed increasingly detailed structural organization (Arasada et al., 2018; Mund et al., 2018; Sochacki et al., 2017), these techniques are not currently able to quantify the dynamics of individual molecules within the endocytic site.
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: Current super-resolution imaging and electron microscopy techniques are not able to quantify the dynamics of individual molecules within the endocytic site.
source: And while recent super-resolution imaging and electron microscopy of CME sites have revealed increasingly detailed structural organization (Arasada et al., 2018; Mund et al., 2018; Sochacki et al., 2017), these techniques are not currently able to quantify the dynamics of individual molecules within the endocytic site.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of current techniques.

claim: Theoretical calculations estimate that the amount of force needed to counteract turgor pressure and invaginate the membrane during CME in yeast is in the range of 1000–3000 pN, or a total energy of 6*10^4 kBT.
source: Theoretical calculations estimate that the amount of force needed to counteract turgor pressure and invaginate the membrane during CME in yeast is in the range of 1000–3000 pN, or a total energy of 6*104 kBT (Carlsson and Bayly, 2014; Dmitrieff and Nédélec, 2015; Lacy et al., 2018; Tweten et al., 2017; Wang and Carlsson, 2017; Ma and Berro, 2019a).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to theoretical modeling studies.

claim: The endocytic actin meshwork is composed of 100–200 short, Arp2/3-branched actin filaments that are capped shortly after nucleation.
source: The endocytic actin meshwork is composed of 100–200 short, Arp2/3-branched actin filaments that are capped shortly after nucleation; quantitative modeling indicates fewer than ten filament ends are polymerizing at any given time (Berro and Pollard, 2014a; Sirotkin et al., 2010), each capable of producing around 1–10 pN of force (Footer et al., 2007; Kovar and Pollard, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior modeling and experimental work.

claim: Quantitative modeling indicates fewer than ten filament ends are polymerizing at any given time in the endocytic actin meshwork.
source: The endocytic actin meshwork is composed of 100–200 short, Arp2/3-branched actin filaments that are capped shortly after nucleation; quantitative modeling indicates fewer than ten filament ends are polymerizing at any given time (Berro and Pollard, 2014a; Sirotkin et al., 2010), each capable of producing around 1–10 pN of force (Footer et al., 2007; Kovar and Pollard, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior modeling work.

claim: Each polymerizing actin filament end is capable of producing around 1–10 pN of force.
source: The endocytic actin meshwork is composed of 100–200 short, Arp2/3-branched actin filaments that are capped shortly after nucleation; quantitative modeling indicates fewer than ten filament ends are polymerizing at any given time (Berro and Pollard, 2014a; Sirotkin et al., 2010), each capable of producing around 1–10 pN of force (Footer et al., 2007; Kovar and Pollard, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior experimental work.

claim: Even after accounting for other force-producing mechanisms, the force from a burst of actin polymerization appears to be insufficient to drive membrane deformation.
source: Even after accounting for other force-producing mechanisms, the force from a burst of actin polymerization appears to be insufficient to drive membrane deformation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of force requirements and force production capacity.

claim: Continuous polymerization and disassembly of actin filaments could allow the meshwork to generate more force than a single burst of filament polymerization.
source: Based on the dendritic nucleation model and theoretical results (Berro et al., 2010), we hypothesized that continuous polymerization and disassembly of actin filaments underlies the observed dynamics in CME, which could allow the meshwork to generate more force than a single burst of filament polymerization.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on prior theoretical work.

claim: Turnover dynamics have been observed in other actin assemblies like lamellipodia.
source: Turnover dynamics have been observed in other actin assemblies like lamellipodia (Pollard and Borisy, 2003; Watanabe and Mitchison, 2002; Yamashiro et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature on lamellipodia.

claim: Fluorescence Recovery After Photobleaching (FRAP) experiments with endocytic actin suggest the endocytic machinery is more dynamic than has been appreciated.
source: Fluorescence Recovery After Photobleaching (FRAP) experiments with endocytic actin (Kaksonen et al., 2003; Kaksonen et al., 2005; Picco et al., 2015) and membrane-coat proteins (Skruzny et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2001) suggest the endocytic machinery is more dynamic than has been appreciated, and previous modeling based on mass action kinetics predicted that the number of molecules for actin nucleators Arp2/3 and WASp consumed over an endocytic event was several times greater than the peak number of molecules present (Berro et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior FRAP studies.

claim: FRAP experiments with membrane-coat proteins suggest the endocytic machinery is more dynamic than has been appreciated.
source: Fluorescence Recovery After Photobleaching (FRAP) experiments with endocytic actin (Kaksonen et al., 2003; Kaksonen et al., 2005; Picco et al., 2015) and membrane-coat proteins (Skruzny et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2001) suggest the endocytic machinery is more dynamic than has been appreciated, and previous modeling based on mass action kinetics predicted that the number of molecules for actin nucleators Arp2/3 and WASp consumed over an endocytic event was several times greater than the peak number of molecules present (Berro et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior FRAP studies.

claim: Previous modeling based on mass action kinetics predicted that the number of molecules for actin nucleators Arp2/3 and WASp consumed over an endocytic event was several times greater than the peak number of molecules present.
source: Fluorescence Recovery After Photobleaching (FRAP) experiments with endocytic actin (Kaksonen et al., 2003; Kaksonen et al., 2005; Picco et al., 2015) and membrane-coat proteins (Skruzny et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2001) suggest the endocytic machinery is more dynamic than has been appreciated, and previous modeling based on mass action kinetics predicted that the number of molecules for actin nucleators Arp2/3 and WASp consumed over an endocytic event was several times greater than the peak number of molecules present (Berro et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior modeling work.

claim: Recent literature generally assumes the endocytic meshwork assembles and disassembles in discrete phases.
source: Recent literature still generally assumes the endocytic meshwork assembles and disassembles in discrete phases and current models take a simplified view of actin turnover, expecting a single phase of assembly followed by disassembly after vesicle formation (Carlsson, 2018; Hassinger et al., 2017; Mund et al., 2018; Picco et al., 2018; Wang and Carlsson, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: Current models take a simplified view of actin turnover, expecting a single phase of assembly followed by disassembly after vesicle formation.
source: Recent literature still generally assumes the endocytic meshwork assembles and disassembles in discrete phases and current models take a simplified view of actin turnover, expecting a single phase of assembly followed by disassembly after vesicle formation (Carlsson, 2018; Hassinger et al., 2017; Mund et al., 2018; Picco et al., 2018; Wang and Carlsson, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent literature.

claim: Continuous turnover of filaments allows a network to sustain high amounts of force production over time.
source: As has been shown in other actin systems, continuous turnover of filaments allows a network to sustain high amounts of force production over time (Craig et al., 2012; Mak et al., 2016; McFadden et al., 2017; Raz-Ben Aroush et al., 2017), converting chemical energy from ATP hydrolysis of actin polymerization into mechanical work over the meshwork's lifetime, among other mechanisms.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on other actin systems.

claim: Continuous turnover converts chemical energy from ATP hydrolysis of actin polymerization into mechanical work over the meshwork's lifetime.
source: As has been shown in other actin systems, continuous turnover of filaments allows a network to sustain high amounts of force production over time (Craig et al., 2012; Mak et al., 2016; McFadden et al., 2017; Raz-Ben Aroush et al., 2017), converting chemical energy from ATP hydrolysis of actin polymerization into mechanical work over the meshwork's lifetime, among other mechanisms.
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation supported by citations.

claim: Recent theoretical work based on the dendritic nucleation model suggests that the endocytic actin meshwork can sustain forces around 2500 pN, sufficient to achieve the membrane invagination.
source: Recent theoretical work based on the dendritic nucleation model, which relies on actin disassembly and turnover, suggests that the endocytic actin meshwork can sustain forces around 2500 pN, sufficient to achieve the membrane invagination (Nickaeen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to recent theoretical work.

claim: Turnover of network components like crosslinkers would enable remodeling of the meshwork, allowing the redistribution of stored elastic energy.
source: Turnover of network components like crosslinkers would also enable remodeling of the meshwork, allowing the redistribution of stored elastic energy (Ma and Berro, 2018; Picco et al., 2018; Ma and Berro, 2019b) and higher order visco-elastic mechanisms.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior theoretical work.

claim: Exchange and turnover of single molecules has not been directly observed in CME because conventional microscopy tools lack the resolution to measure such behavior within a transient and diffraction-limited structure like the endocytic patch.
source: However, exchange and turnover of single molecules has not been directly observed in CME because conventional microscopy tools lack the resolution to measure such behavior within a transient and diffraction-limited structure like the endocytic patch.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of prior experimental approaches.

claim: The study applied a variation of single-molecule speckle microscopy to track individual molecules in CME sites in live fission yeast.
source: In this study, we applied a variation of single-molecule speckle microscopy to track individual molecules in CME sites in live fission yeast.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Eight target proteins were analyzed, including actin-meshwork and membrane-coat proteins.
source: For eight target proteins, including actin-meshwork and membrane-coat proteins, we sparsely labeled the proteins in the cell and applied single-molecule localization and tracking analyses.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: The results provide direct evidence for rapid and continuous turnover of the endocytic meshwork on the timescale of 1–2 s.
source: These results provide direct evidence for rapid and continuous turnover of the endocytic meshwork on the timescale of 1–2 s, and their motions reveal heterogeneous behaviors at the molecular level.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: The motions of endocytic proteins reveal heterogeneous behaviors at the molecular level.
source: These results provide direct evidence for rapid and continuous turnover of the endocytic meshwork on the timescale of 1–2 s, and their motions reveal heterogeneous behaviors at the molecular level.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of single-molecule tracking data.

claim: This observation verifies a key behavior of how the endocytic actin meshwork is able to generate and sustain forces to remodel the membrane in CME.
source: This observation verifies a key behavior of how the endocytic actin meshwork is able to generate and sustain forces to remodel the membrane in CME.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the significance of the findings.

claim: Different hypothetical mechanisms can generate similar bulk measurements in CME.
source: Different hypothetical mechanisms can generate similar bulk measurements
evidence: This is demonstrated through the logical simulations presented in Figure 1.

claim: A common interpretation of previous endocytic patch intensity tracking data is that the actin monomers and associated proteins polymerize into a meshwork during the CCP invagination and then gradually disassemble after the vesicle is pinched off.
source: A common interpretation of previous endocytic patch intensity tracking data is that the actin monomers and associated proteins polymerize into a meshwork during the CCP invagination and then gradually disassemble after the vesicle is pinched off.
evidence: This is a statement about the prevailing interpretation in the field.

claim: The apparent time-course of endocytic actin could result from a dynamic structure with continuous turnover where net growth and net disassembly are achieved by altering the balance between nucleation/polymerization and disassembly rates.
source: We hypothesized that the apparent time-course of endocytic actin could result from a dynamic structure with continuous turnover where net growth and net disassembly are achieved by altering the balance between nucleation/polymerization and disassembly rates.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: Logical simulations demonstrate that fundamentally different models as all-in-one assembly or continuous turnover could each generate apparent dynamics that resemble previously observed microscopy data.
source: We first performed basic logical simulations to illustrate that such fundamentally different models as all-in-one assembly or continuous turnover could each generate apparent dynamics that resemble previously observed microscopy data (Figure 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated through simulations shown in Figure 1.

claim: In the discrete assembly models the peak number of molecules contains all of the molecules that participated, while the continuous turnover model consumes a total number of molecules several times greater than the peak number.
source: Importantly, in the discrete assembly models the peak number of molecules contains all of the molecules that participated, while the continuous turnover model consumes a total number of molecules several times greater than the peak number (Figure 1C, right).
evidence: This is shown in the simulation results in Figure 1C.

claim: Acp1p-mEGFP endocytic patches have lifetimes of 18.4 ± 3.5 s (mean ± S.D.).
source: We first imaged cells expressing mEGFP-tagged heterodimeric actin capping protein subunit Acp1p in partial-TIRF and tracked endocytic patches, measuring lifetimes of 18.4 ± 3.5 s (mean ± S.D., Figure 2A–C, Table 1, and Figure 2—video 1), consistent with previous reports of capping protein lifetimes (Berro and Pollard, 2014a; Sirotkin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a direct measurement from the experiments shown in Figure 2 and Table 1.

claim: The measured Acp1p-mEGFP patch lifetimes are consistent with previous reports of capping protein lifetimes.
source: We first imaged cells expressing mEGFP-tagged heterodimeric actin capping protein subunit Acp1p in partial-TIRF and tracked endocytic patches, measuring lifetimes of 18.4 ± 3.5 s (mean ± S.D., Figure 2A–C, Table 1, and Figure 2—video 1), consistent with previous reports of capping protein lifetimes (Berro and Pollard, 2014a; Sirotkin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior literature.

claim: For Myo1p, Wsp1p, Acp1p, and Fim1p, the recovery of fluorescence after photobleaching was very fast.
source: For all four proteins, the recovery of fluorescence after photobleaching was very fast (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1, and Figure 2—video 2, Figure 2—video 3, Figure 2—video 4, Figure 2—video 5), demonstrating that these proteins exchange rapidly during the assembly and the disassembly stages of endocytic structures.
evidence: This is a finding from FRAP experiments shown in Figure 2D and supplementary figures.

claim: Myo1p, Wsp1p, Acp1p, and Fim1p exchange rapidly during the assembly and the disassembly stages of endocytic structures.
source: For all four proteins, the recovery of fluorescence after photobleaching was very fast (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1, and Figure 2—video 2, Figure 2—video 3, Figure 2—video 4, Figure 2—video 5), demonstrating that these proteins exchange rapidly during the assembly and the disassembly stages of endocytic structures.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the FRAP data.

claim: The recovery half-times for Myo1p, Wsp1p, Acp1p, and Fim1p are estimated to be on the order of 1 s.
source: However, we estimate from our data that the recovery half-times are on the order of 1 s, as the intensity typically reaches the pre-bleached value within 1 to 2 s.
evidence: This is an estimate from the FRAP data.

claim: The fraction of fluorescence recovered after photobleaching is very large (close to 100%) for Myo1p, Wsp1p, Acp1p, and Fim1p.
source: The fraction recovered is very large (close to 100%) for all four proteins, and the fluorescence intensity reaches a peak value similar to the peak in unbleached traces (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the FRAP experiments.

claim: Incubating live fission yeast with low concentrations of SNAP-substrate dye achieves only a low labeling efficiency, enabling single-molecule tracking.
source: As reported in Lacy et al. (2017), incubating live fission yeast with low concentrations of SNAP-substrate dye achieves only a low labeling efficiency (see Materials and methods), enabling single-molecule tracking because typically one or zero of these sparsely labeled molecules are incorporated into diffraction-limited CME sites.
evidence: This is a methodological finding supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Spots observed after SNAP-SiR labeling colocalize specifically with endocytic sites.
source: We confirmed that the spots observed after SNAP-SiR labeling colocalize specifically with endocytic sites by imaging a strain co-expressing Acp2p-mEGFP and the endocytic actin crosslinker Fim1p-SNAP labeled with SNAP-SiR, and we observed negligible non-specific binding of SNAP-SiR dye in wild-type cells expressing no SNAP-tag (Figure 2—figure supplement 2, Figure 3—video 10).
evidence: This is a validation experiment shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: There is negligible non-specific binding of SNAP-SiR dye in wild-type cells expressing no SNAP-tag.
source: We confirmed that the spots observed after SNAP-SiR labeling colocalize specifically with endocytic sites by imaging a strain co-expressing Acp2p-mEGFP and the endocytic actin crosslinker Fim1p-SNAP labeled with SNAP-SiR, and we observed negligible non-specific binding of SNAP-SiR dye in wild-type cells expressing no SNAP-tag (Figure 2—figure supplement 2, Figure 3—video 10).
evidence: This is a control experiment shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: In Acp1p-mEGFP cells, 70 to 120 endocytic events occur per cell at any time.
source: In contrast to the many endocytic patches visible in Acp1p-mEGFP cells (70 to 120 endocytic events occurring per cell at any time Berro and Pollard, 2014a), we observe only a few spots in cells expressing Acp1p-SNAP sparsely labeled with SNAP-SiR (referred to as Acp1p-SiR), typically 5 to 10 labeled molecules per cell per minute (Figure 3—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: In cells expressing Acp1p-SNAP sparsely labeled with SNAP-SiR, typically 5 to 10 labeled molecules per cell per minute are observed.
source: In contrast to the many endocytic patches visible in Acp1p-mEGFP cells (70 to 120 endocytic events occurring per cell at any time Berro and Pollard, 2014a), we observe only a few spots in cells expressing Acp1p-SNAP sparsely labeled with SNAP-SiR (referred to as Acp1p-SiR), typically 5 to 10 labeled molecules per cell per minute (Figure 3—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experiments.

claim: Acp1p-SiR spots had short lifetimes in a peaked distribution with a long tail, with average 1.4 s and 95% of events under 3.6 s.
source: Strikingly, Acp1p-SiR spots had short lifetimes in a peaked distribution with a long tail, with average 1.4 s and 95% of events under 3.6 s (Figure 2F–G).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule tracking experiments shown in Figure 2F-G.

claim: GFP-tagged versions of actin-associated proteins (Act1p, Acp1p, Fim1p, and Arc5p) have been previously reported to have bulk lifetimes in CME sites around 20–25 s.
source: GFP-tagged versions of actin-associated proteins (Act1p, Acp1p, Fim1p, and Arc5p) have been previously reported to have bulk lifetimes in CME sites around 20–25 s (Picco et al., 2015; Sirotkin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Single-molecule tracks of Act1p, Acp1p, Fim1p, and Arc5p tagged with SNAP-SiR display short lifetimes averaging 1.4 to 1.6 s.
source: Single-molecule tracks of these proteins tagged with SNAP-SiR display short lifetimes averaging 1.4 to 1.6 s (Figure 3 and Table 2), while Wsp1p displays even shorter lifetimes (mean = 1.15 s, 95%ile = 2.6 s).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule tracking experiments shown in Figure 3 and Table 2.

claim: Wsp1p displays even shorter lifetimes than other actin-associated proteins (mean = 1.15 s, 95%ile = 2.6 s).
source: Single-molecule tracks of these proteins tagged with SNAP-SiR display short lifetimes averaging 1.4 to 1.6 s (Figure 3 and Table 2), while Wsp1p displays even shorter lifetimes (mean = 1.15 s, 95%ile = 2.6 s).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule tracking experiments shown in Figure 3 and Table 2.

claim: End4p and Clc1p have been reported to have bulk lifetimes around 40 s and 110 s.
source: End4p and Clc1p, which have been reported to have bulk lifetimes around 40 s and 110 s (Sirotkin et al., 2010) also display short average single-molecule residence times of 1.6 and 1.5 s, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: End4p and Clc1p display short average single-molecule residence times of 1.6 and 1.5 s, respectively.
source: End4p and Clc1p, which have been reported to have bulk lifetimes around 40 s and 110 s (Sirotkin et al., 2010) also display short average single-molecule residence times of 1.6 and 1.5 s, respectively.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the single-molecule tracking experiments.

claim: All of the target proteins display a similar shape of residence time distribution, except for Fim1p, which contains a unique sub-population of short-lived events around 0.5 s.
source: All of the target proteins display a similar shape of residence time distribution, except for Fim1p, which contains a unique sub-population of short-lived events around 0.5 s.
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis of residence time distributions.

claim: Small but statistically significant differences occur between the distributions of lifetimes for many samples.
source: Small but statistically significant differences occur between the distributions of lifetimes for many samples (by Mann-Whitney test, Figure 3—figure supplement 2), with Fim1p and Wsp1p significantly different from all other samples (at p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis result shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Fim1p and Wsp1p are significantly different from all other samples in their lifetime distributions (at p<0.0001).
source: Small but statistically significant differences occur between the distributions of lifetimes for many samples (by Mann-Whitney test, Figure 3—figure supplement 2), with Fim1p and Wsp1p significantly different from all other samples (at p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis result.

claim: All samples except for Arc5p are significantly different from Pil1p in their lifetime distributions (at p<0.05).
source: All samples except for Arc5p are significantly different from Pil1p (at p<0.05).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis result.

claim: All of the endocytic proteins measured display much shorter lifetime than would be predicted for a simple assembly/disassembly model given their bulk lifetimes that have been reported previously.
source: All of the endocytic proteins we measured display much shorter lifetime than would be predicted for a simple assembly/disassembly model given their bulk lifetimes that have been reported previously (Berro and Pollard, 2014a; Sirotkin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a comparison between the new findings and predictions from simple models.

claim: The disappearance of spots is attributed to dissociation of labeled proteins from endocytic sites, and not to photobleaching or other photophysical artifacts.
source: We attribute the disappearance of spots to dissociation of labeled proteins from endocytic sites, and not to photobleaching or other photophysical artifacts.
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by control experiments.

claim: Increasing illumination intensity caused a corresponding increase in the global photobleaching rate (0.12 sec−1 to 0.18 sec−1), but the distributions of track lifetimes did not change significantly.
source: While increasing illumination intensity caused a corresponding increase in the global photobleaching rate as measured by the decay in the number of spots visible per frame (0.12 sec−1 to 0.18 sec−1), the distributions of track lifetimes did not change significantly (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Table 3, Figure 3—video 9).
evidence: This is a control experiment shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Table 3.

claim: In images of Acp1p-SiR cells fixed with paraformaldehyde, many fluorescent spots could be tracked over 15 s long under the same imaging conditions and recording settings.
source: Additionally, in images of Acp1p-SiR cells fixed with paraformaldehyde, we could track many fluorescent spots over 15 s long under the same imaging conditions and recording settings (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, Table 3, Figure 2—video 7).
evidence: This is a control experiment shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and Table 3.

claim: Photobleaching occurs about ten-fold slower than the spot lifetimes measured and is not interfering with the ability to track single fluorophores.
source: Therefore, while photobleaching does occur during the imaging time, it is about ten-fold slower than the spot lifetimes we measured and is not interfering with our ability to track single fluorophores.
evidence: This is an inference from the comparison of photobleaching rates and track lifetimes.

claim: The single-molecule tracks typically span a net distance of only 100 to 200 nm.
source: The single-molecule tracks typically span a net distance of only 100 to 200 nm (Figure 4A), that is the distance traveled from the first appearance of a spot to its disappearance.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of track displacements shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Actin-associated proteins and clathrin contain a greater proportion of long tracks (>250 nm).
source: Actin-associated proteins and clathrin contain a greater proportion of long tracks (>250 nm, Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Most of the differences between different proteins' distributions of track distances are statistically significant (at p<0.05).
source: By two sample Mann-Whitney test, most of the differences between different proteins' distributions of track distances are statistically significant (at p<0.05, Figure 3—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis result shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E.

claim: For molecules undergoing pure diffusive motion, the net distance increases with the square root of the lifetime.
source: For molecules undergoing pure diffusive motion, the net distance increases with the square root of the lifetime.
evidence: This is a statement of physical principles.

claim: Net distances depend on lifetime only for some proteins.
source: However, we observed net distances depend on lifetime only for some proteins (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Long-lived tracks of actin-associated proteins (Act1p, Acp1p, Fim1p, and Arc5p) travel longer distance than short-lived tracks.
source: Comparing the tracks in the top and bottom 10% of lifetimes shows that long-lived tracks of actin-associated proteins (Act1p, Acp1p, Fim1p, and Arc5p) travel longer distance than short-lived tracks (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: For membrane-bound endocytic proteins (Myo1p, Wsp1p, End4p, and to some extent, Clc1p) the dependence of distance on lifetime is lost.
source: For membrane-bound endocytic proteins (Myo1p, Wsp1p, End4p, and to some extent, Clc1p) this dependence is lost (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Pil1p displays overall short displacements with a median track length of 134 nm, likely limited by the localization precision.
source: Pil1p displays overall short displacements with a median track length of 134 nm, likely limited by the localization precision.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis with an interpretation about the limitation.

claim: For all the endocytic proteins the MSD is linear at short time scales, suggesting diffusive behavior, but appears sub-diffusive at longer timescales.
source: For all the endocytic proteins the MSD is linear at short time scales, suggesting diffusive behavior, but appears sub-diffusive at longer timescales (not shown here, but see Figure 6).
evidence: This is a finding from the MSD analysis.

claim: Tracks of actin-associated proteins and clathrin have higher apparent mobility (2,700 to 3,800 nm2/sec) than those of membrane-associated proteins Myo1p, Wsp1p, and End4p (1,300 to 1,800 nm2/sec).
source: Tracks of actin-associated proteins and clathrin have higher apparent mobility (2,700 to 3,800 nm2/sec) than those of membrane-associated proteins Myo1p, Wsp1p, and End4p (1,300 to 1,800 nm2/sec).
evidence: This is a finding from the diffusion coefficient analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Membrane-associated endocytic proteins Myo1p, Wsp1p, and End4p display higher average mobility than Pil1p (~500 nm2/sec).
source: However, these less-mobile endocytic proteins still display higher average mobility than Pil1p (~500 nm2/sec), indicative of nanoscale motions within the CME membrane patch.
evidence: This is a finding from the diffusion coefficient analysis.

claim: The higher mobility of membrane-associated endocytic proteins compared to Pil1p is indicative of nanoscale motions within the CME membrane patch.
source: However, these less-mobile endocytic proteins still display higher average mobility than Pil1p (~500 nm2/sec), indicative of nanoscale motions within the CME membrane patch.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mobility data.

claim: High-mobility events have an average apparent D of 6,050 ± 720 nm2/sec.
source: Across the full datasets grouped in this way, high-mobility events have an average apparent D of 6,050 ± 720 nm2/sec, mid-mobility events correspond to apparent D of 1,100 ± 14 nm2/sec, and low-mobility events correspond to apparent D of 67 ± 35 nm2/sec.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of mobility classes.

claim: Mid-mobility events correspond to apparent D of 1,100 ± 14 nm2/sec.
source: Across the full datasets grouped in this way, high-mobility events have an average apparent D of 6,050 ± 720 nm2/sec, mid-mobility events correspond to apparent D of 1,100 ± 14 nm2/sec, and low-mobility events correspond to apparent D of 67 ± 35 nm2/sec.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of mobility classes.

claim: Low-mobility events correspond to apparent D of 67 ± 35 nm2/sec.
source: Across the full datasets grouped in this way, high-mobility events have an average apparent D of 6,050 ± 720 nm2/sec, mid-mobility events correspond to apparent D of 1,100 ± 14 nm2/sec, and low-mobility events correspond to apparent D of 67 ± 35 nm2/sec.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of mobility classes.

claim: The high-, mid-, and low-mobility behaviors are consistent with vesicle diffusion, motions within the CCP-associated meshwork, and membrane-bound states, respectively.
source: The high-, mid-, and low-mobility behaviors shown in Figure 6 (average apparent D for each class ~6,000 nm2/sec, ~1,100 nm2/sec, ~65 nm2/sec) are consistent with vesicle diffusion, motions within the CCP-associated meshwork, and membrane-bound states, respectively.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mobility classes.

claim: The longer distances traveled by some tracks of actin-associated proteins are attributed to molecules that remain associated with the endocytic vesicle after scission.
source: We attribute the longer distances traveled by some tracks of actin-associated proteins (Figure 4C, Figure 6) to be molecules that remain associated with the endocytic vesicle after scission.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the tracking data.

claim: The large majority of events have very short end-to-end distance.
source: However, the large majority of events have very short end-to-end distance (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: The apparent over-representation of events with restricted motions is consistent with a switch in behavior of the CME assembly from rapid turnover with small motions in the developing CCP to reduced recruitment and sustained disassembly around the vesicle after scission.
source: This apparent over-representation of events with restricted motions is consistent with a switch in behavior of the CME assembly from rapid turnover with small motions in the developing CCP to reduced recruitment and sustained disassembly around the vesicle after scission.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the motion data.

claim: Unique sub-populations are apparent in several proteins' behaviors, suggesting various motions for long- or short-lived components of the CME meshwork.
source: Unique sub-populations are apparent in several proteins' behaviors (Figure 6), suggesting various motions for long- or short-lived components of the CME meshwork.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the heterogeneity observed in Figure 6.

claim: For all proteins, very long-timescale events (>10 s) generally exhibit only short displacements, indicating that these molecules are restricted to small motions on the CCP membrane and are disassembled from the diffusing CCV relatively quickly.
source: For all proteins, very long-timescale events (>10 s) generally exhibit only short displacements, indicating that these molecules are restricted to small motions on the CCP membrane and are disassembled from the diffusing CCV relatively quickly.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the long-lived track behavior.

claim: The results of single-molecule tracking are sensitive to the chosen tracking parameters.
source: We acknowledge that the results of single-molecule tracking are sensitive to the chosen tracking parameters (Jaqaman et al., 2008; Smith et al., 2011), especially because the images' low signal-to-background ratio results in some missed detections of spots.
evidence: This is a statement about methodological considerations supported by citations.

claim: Even across a broad range of parameters up to unrealistic values that introduce verifiable artifacts, the average single-molecule residence times remain below 3 to 4 s.
source: However, even across a broad range of parameters up to unrealistic values that introduce verifiable artifacts, the average single-molecule residence times remain below 3 to 4 s (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), still much faster than the ~10 s prediction for single-turnover mechanisms (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the parameter sensitivity analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The average single-molecule residence times are much faster than the ~10 s prediction for single-turnover mechanisms.
source: However, even across a broad range of parameters up to unrealistic values that introduce verifiable artifacts, the average single-molecule residence times remain below 3 to 4 s (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), still much faster than the ~10 s prediction for single-turnover mechanisms (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a comparison between the measured data and model predictions.

claim: The results support the idea that the actin network can remodel during CME and generate greater total force than has been previously estimated.
source: Our results have important qualitative and quantitative implications for models of the endocytic machinery. They support the idea that the actin network can remodel during CME and generate greater total force than has been previously estimated.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the implications of the findings.

claim: Previous discussions of CME often assumed that the entire actin meshwork and membrane coat assembles and disassembles once during the total lifetime of the patch.
source: Previous discussions of CME often assumed that the entire actin meshwork and membrane coat assembles and disassembles once during the total lifetime of the patch, with 'turnover' referring to the release of proteins to be re-used in a later CME event.
evidence: This is a statement about the prevailing assumptions in the field.

claim: Discrete phases of assembly and disassembly of actin monomers (and associated proteins) would result in an average residence time of ~10 s.
source: Discrete phases of assembly and disassembly of actin monomers (and associated proteins) would result in an average residence time of ~10 s (Figure 1), inconsistent with our results.
evidence: This is a prediction from the model shown in Figure 1.

claim: Current literature still generally assumes the endocytic meshwork assembles and disassembles in discrete phases.
source: Although some earlier reports have suggested the existence of turnover within the CME machinery, current literature still generally assumes the endocytic meshwork assembles and disassembles in discrete phases (Carlsson, 2018; Hassinger et al., 2017; Mund et al., 2018; Picco et al., 2018; Wang and Carlsson, 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of the field supported by citations.

claim: If more total molecules of actin are consumed by the endocytic meshwork, the total chemical energy of polymerization released through ATP hydrolysis must be several times higher than has been previously estimated.
source: If more total molecules of actin are consumed by the endocytic meshwork, the total chemical energy of polymerization released through ATP hydrolysis must be several times higher than has been previously estimated.
evidence: This is an inference about the energetic implications of the findings.

claim: To accumulate the known peak number of actin molecules while sustaining such a high rate of turnover, the rates of polymerization and disassembly must both be higher than previously estimated.
source: To accumulate the known peak number of actin molecules while sustaining such a high rate of turnover (consuming up to five times more actin), the rates of polymerization and disassembly must both be higher than previously estimated, and turnover of the actin-nucleation promoting factors Wsp1p and Myo1p would generate a higher number of polymerizing ends over the lifetime of the CME event.
evidence: This is an inference about the kinetic implications of the findings.

claim: Turnover of the actin-nucleation promoting factors Wsp1p and Myo1p would generate a higher number of polymerizing ends over the lifetime of the CME event.
source: To accumulate the known peak number of actin molecules while sustaining such a high rate of turnover (consuming up to five times more actin), the rates of polymerization and disassembly must both be higher than previously estimated, and turnover of the actin-nucleation promoting factors Wsp1p and Myo1p would generate a higher number of polymerizing ends over the lifetime of the CME event.
evidence: This is an inference about the implications for nucleation.

claim: The endocytic patch contains approximately 6,500 actin monomers at its peak.
source: The endocytic patch contains approximately 6,500 actin monomers at its peak (Sirotkin et al., 2010) MBoC, Berro 2010 MBoC), but based on the residence times we report here, a single patch might consume more than 30,000 actin subunits over time.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Based on the residence times reported, a single patch might consume more than 30,000 actin subunits over time.
source: The endocytic patch contains approximately 6,500 actin monomers at its peak (Sirotkin et al., 2010) MBoC, Berro 2010 MBoC), but based on the residence times we report here, a single patch might consume more than 30,000 actin subunits over time.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the measured residence times and known peak numbers.

claim: A recent report proposed that myosin-Is enable higher rates of actin polymerization by pushing the filament ends away from the membrane.
source: A recent report proposed that myosin-Is (Myo3 and Myo5 in budding yeast) enable higher rates of actin polymerization by pushing the filament ends away from the membrane (Manenschijn et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to recent literature.

claim: Mechanical stress in highly-crosslinked actin networks can greatly enhance the rate of ADF/cofilin severing of actin filaments.
source: Another recent report demonstrated that mechanical stress in highly-crosslinked actin networks can greatly enhance the rate of ADF/cofilin severing of actin filaments (Wioland et al., 2019), which could also contribute to the high turnover rates we observe in CME patches.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to recent literature.

claim: Mechanical stress in highly-crosslinked actin networks could contribute to the high turnover rates observed in CME patches.
source: Another recent report demonstrated that mechanical stress in highly-crosslinked actin networks can greatly enhance the rate of ADF/cofilin severing of actin filaments (Wioland et al., 2019), which could also contribute to the high turnover rates we observe in CME patches.
evidence: This is a speculation about a mechanism that could explain the findings.

claim: Fast turnover of the actin meshwork components could affect other higher-order mechanisms of force generation.
source: Fast turnover of the actin meshwork components could affect other higher-order mechanisms of force generation.
evidence: This is a speculation about broader implications.

claim: Continuous unbinding of fimbrin crosslinkers would allow remodeling of the meshwork and spatiotemporal redistribution of elastic energy stored in crosslinkers.
source: For example, continuous unbinding of fimbrin crosslinkers would allow remodeling of the meshwork and spatiotemporal redistribution of elastic energy stored in crosslinkers (Ma and Berro, 2018; Ma and Berro, 2019b; Picco et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculation supported by citations to prior theoretical work.

claim: Remodeling of the actin meshwork could enable important changes in the orientation of filaments and their forces over time.
source: Such remodeling of the actin meshwork could also enable important changes in the orientation of filaments and their forces over time.
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional implications of remodeling.

claim: Nickaeen et al. (2019) reported simulations based on the dendritic nucleation model indicating that the endocytic actin meshwork can sustain forces sufficient to achieve the membrane invagination.
source: While our paper was in preparation, Nickaeen et al. (2019) reported simulations based on the dendritic nucleation model, which requires actin disassembly and turnover, indicating that the endocytic actin meshwork can sustain forces sufficient to achieve the membrane invagination.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to recent theoretical work.

claim: The results are a key experimental validation of the predicted turnover behavior, which was not directly accessible in previous experimental and theoretical studies.
source: Our results are a key experimental validation of this predicted turnover behavior, which was not directly accessible in previous experimental and theoretical studies.
evidence: This is a statement about the significance of the findings.

claim: Future studies of CME should consider the endocytic actin meshwork and membrane coat as highly dynamic, turning over multiple times to generate, distribute, and transmit the forces that deform the plasma membrane into a vesicle.
source: Future studies of CME should consider the endocytic actin meshwork and membrane coat as highly dynamic, turning over multiple times to generate, distribute, and transmit the forces that deform the plasma membrane into a vesicle.
evidence: This is a recommendation for future research based on the findings.

claim: Novel experimental methods will be needed to measure rates and identify specific molecular complexes at the endocytic site.
source: Novel experimental methods will be needed to measure rates and identify specific molecular complexes at the endocytic site.
evidence: This is a statement about future research needs.

claim: The increasing accessibility of super-resolution microscopy and single-molecule techniques as well as added levels of detail in computational models will enable further exploration of the molecular mechanisms of CME and other complex molecular assemblies in live cells.
source: We expect that the increasing accessibility of super-resolution microscopy and single-molecule techniques as well as added levels of detail in computational models will enable further exploration of the molecular mechanisms of CME and other complex molecular assemblies in live cells.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research directions.

claim: The characteristic shape of residence time distributions (a peak with a skewed tail) indicates that the unbinding dynamics of these proteins do not follow a simple kinetic mechanism.
source: The characteristic shape of these residence time distributions, a peak with a skewed tail, indicates that the unbinding dynamics of these proteins do not follow a simple kinetic mechanism.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the shape of the distributions.

claim: Mass action kinetics predict an exponential distribution for single-step unbinding mechanism.
source: Mass action kinetics predict an exponential distribution for single-step unbinding mechanism.
evidence: This is a statement of theoretical principles.

claim: Multi-step kinetic pathways result in residence times (or 'dwell times') following a gamma distribution.
source: In general, multi-step kinetic pathways result in residence times (or 'dwell times') following a gamma distribution (Floyd et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior theoretical work.

claim: The residence times of actin monomers in a treadmilling filament have been shown to follow complex kinetics resulting in a peak shape that depends on all of the rates of polymerization, aging, cofilin binding, and severing steps.
source: Correspondingly, the residence times of actin monomers in a treadmilling filament have been shown to follow complex kinetics resulting in a peak shape that depends on all of the rates of polymerization, aging, cofilin binding, and severing steps (Roland et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work on actin dynamics.

claim: The shapes of the residence time distributions appear similar to models of multi-step kinetics.
source: Although we have not extracted specific rate constants from our data, the shapes of the residence time distributions appear similar to those models.
evidence: This is a qualitative comparison to theoretical models.

claim: The skewed peak shape argues against the interpretation that these single-molecule events arise from transient associations with stable assemblies.
source: The skewed peak shape also argues against the interpretation that these single-molecule events arise from transient associations with stable assemblies, which would instead result in exponential dwell time distributions by mass-action kinetics.
evidence: This is an inference ruling out an alternative interpretation.

claim: The dissociation kinetics for actin-associated proteins are likely driven by the disassembly and severing of the actin filaments to which they are bound rather than simple unbinding.
source: The dissociation kinetics for actin-associated proteins are likely driven by the disassembly and severing of the actin filaments to which they are bound rather than simple unbinding, because the unbinding rates measured for these proteins in vitro are typically far slower than the timescales we observed here.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on comparison to in vitro measurements.

claim: Unbinding rates from actin filaments have been reported for Acp1p in the range of 10−4 sec−1.
source: For example, unbinding rates from actin filaments have been reported for Acp1p in the range of 10−4 sec−1 (Bombardier et al., 2015; Kuhn and Pollard, 2007) and for Fim1p in the range of 10−2 to 10−3 sec−1 (Skau et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior in vitro studies.

claim: Unbinding rates from actin filaments have been reported for Fim1p in the range of 10−2 to 10−3 sec−1.
source: For example, unbinding rates from actin filaments have been reported for Acp1p in the range of 10−4 sec−1 (Bombardier et al., 2015; Kuhn and Pollard, 2007) and for Fim1p in the range of 10−2 to 10−3 sec−1 (Skau et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior in vitro studies.

claim: The slight differences between residence times of actin-associated proteins may reflect the delay of binding a filament only after its nucleation.
source: The slight differences between residence times of actin-associated proteins may reflect the delay of binding a filament only after its nucleation (as Fim1p and Acp1p residence times are slightly shorter than Act1p), or the additional time for pre-recruitment before nucleation of the actin branch (as Arc5p residence times are slightly longer than Act1p).
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanistic basis for differences.

claim: The fast sub-population of Fim1p tracks around 0.5 s may correspond to transient binding events that engage one but not both actin-binding domains before unbinding.
source: The fast sub-population of Fim1p tracks around 0.5 s may correspond to transient binding events that engage one but not both actin-binding domains before unbinding; such a prominent population of transient events is absent in other proteins.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanistic basis for the Fim1p sub-population.

claim: The similar shape and timescale for residence times of membrane-associated proteins might be explained by unique combinations of rates governing those proteins' interactions with the membrane and many binding partners.
source: The similar shape and timescale for residence times of membrane-associated proteins might be explained by other unique combinations of rates governing those proteins' interactions with the membrane and many binding partners, especially in oligomeric lattice assemblies such as the clathrin coat.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanistic basis for membrane protein kinetics.

claim: The short lifetimes measured for clathrin agree with previous reports that individual clathrin triskelia unbind during CCP development in order to achieve the necessary change in curvature.
source: The short lifetimes we measured for clathrin (Clc1p) agree with previous reports that individual clathrin triskelia unbind during CCP development in order to achieve the necessary change in curvature (Avinoam et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior literature.

claim: Previous studies reported that WASp rapidly exchanges at sites of actin nucleation.
source: Previous studies also reported that WASp rapidly exchanges at sites of actin nucleation (Weisswange et al., 2009), although these dynamics have not been measured directly in CME.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Considerably fewer long-lived immobile events are observed for Clc1p than for End4p, suggesting that clathrin turns over throughout the CCP lifetime and not exclusively during late stages of membrane invagination.
source: While both End4p and Clc1p are known to reside at endocytic sites long before CCP invagination and scission (bulk lifetimes around 40 s and 110 s, respectively Sirotkin et al., 2010), we observe considerably fewer long-lived immobile events for Clc1p than for End4p (Figure 6), suggesting that clathrin turns over throughout the CCP lifetime and not exclusively during late stages of membrane invagination.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Consistent with its proposed role in anchoring the actin meshwork with the CCP membrane, End4p displays the highest fraction of long-lived events compared with other endocytic proteins.
source: Consistent with its proposed role in anchoring the actin meshwork with the CCP membrane, End4p (Sla2 in budding yeast) displays the highest fraction of long-lived events compared with other endocytic proteins.
evidence: This is an interpretation relating the data to the known function of End4p.

claim: Polymerized actin at CME sites moves away from the cell membrane at approximately 50 nm/sec.
source: Kaksonen and colleagues have used photobleaching experiments in mutant yeast strains which generate long actin comet-tails to determine that the polymerized actin at CME sites moves away from the cell membrane at approximately 50 nm/sec (Kaksonen et al., 2003), and single-molecule tracking measurements of actin in lamellipodia report retrograde flow around 30 nm/sec (Yamashiro et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Single-molecule tracking measurements of actin in lamellipodia report retrograde flow around 30 nm/sec.
source: Kaksonen and colleagues have used photobleaching experiments in mutant yeast strains which generate long actin comet-tails to determine that the polymerized actin at CME sites moves away from the cell membrane at approximately 50 nm/sec (Kaksonen et al., 2003), and single-molecule tracking measurements of actin in lamellipodia report retrograde flow around 30 nm/sec (Yamashiro et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Electron microscopy studies have shown that the size of the endocytic actin meshwork extends about 100 to 250 nm from the cell membrane.
source: Electron microscopy studies have shown that the size of the endocytic actin meshwork extends about 100 to 250 nm from the cell membrane (Idrissi et al., 2012; Kukulski et al., 2012) and mathematical modeling has shown that the endocytic actin filaments are typically 100 to 150 nm long (Berro et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior EM studies.

claim: Mathematical modeling has shown that the endocytic actin filaments are typically 100 to 150 nm long.
source: Electron microscopy studies have shown that the size of the endocytic actin meshwork extends about 100 to 250 nm from the cell membrane (Idrissi et al., 2012; Kukulski et al., 2012) and mathematical modeling has shown that the endocytic actin filaments are typically 100 to 150 nm long (Berro et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior modeling work.

claim: The partly overlapping presence of actin assembly and disassembly factors in endocytic patches has suggested that actin monomers could travel the distance of the meshwork and turn over as rapidly as every 3 to 5 s.
source: These findings, along with the partly overlapping presence of actin assembly and disassembly factors in endocytic patches, have suggested that actin monomers could travel the distance of the meshwork and turn over as rapidly as every 3 to 5 s (Goode et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: The single-molecule data are the first direct observation that actin and associated proteins have typical single-molecule residence times around 1 to 2 s, and indeed rarely reside at an endocytic site longer than 3 s.
source: Consistent with those estimates and our own FRAP experiments, our single-molecule data are now the first direct observation that actin and associated proteins have typical single-molecule residence times around 1 to 2 s, and indeed rarely reside at an endocytic site longer than 3 s (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a statement of the primary finding and its significance.
